author: original (NevaIB)
title: Regression of x on y

points.text: The regression line of x on y
Choosing the right line for a prediction

bigPicture: There are two regression lines. Use y on x to predict y, and x on y to predict x; both pass through the mean point.

keyIdeas.cue: What is the regression line of x on y?
keyIdeas.answer: x = cy + d, found on the GDC by entering y as the independent (first) list. It minimises horizontal distances, so it differs from the y-on-x line unless |r| = 1. Both lines pass through (x̄, ȳ).

keyIdeas.cue: Which line should you use for a prediction?
keyIdeas.answer: To predict y from a given x: the y-on-x line. To predict x from a given y: the x-on-y line. Never rearrange the y-on-x line to predict x.

keyTerms.term: regression line of x on y
keyTerms.def: line for predicting x from y

workedExamples.title: Choose the line
workedExamples.prompt: Arm span y and height x have y-on-x line y = 0.98x + 2 and x-on-y line x = 0.95y + 5. Predict height for arm span 170 cm.
steps: predicting x from y: use x on y

misconceptions.wrong: Rearrange y = ax + b to get x
The two lines are the same line

practice.prompt: The regression line of y on x is y = 2x + 3 and the regression line of x on y is x = 0.4y − 0.2. (a) Find the mean point. (b) Estimate x when y = 20.
Using x: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 and y: 15, 22, 24, 31, 35, 41, find the regression line of x on y and estimate x when y = 30.
solution: GDC LinReg with y as the first list
commonErrors: Using the y-on-x line rearranged (gives 6.61 only by luck when r ≈ 1)
Entering the lists in the wrong order

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
